feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the technical/strategic blend is compelling. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with tighter formatting, fewer repeated skill sections, and more quantified outcomes beyond activity/scope metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and broad platform/tool expertise.  
- Writing is professional and readable, with a consistent leadership narrative across digital strategy, governance, content operations, and multimedia.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would sharpen structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-driven achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results such as growth %, efficiency gains, engagement improvements, or cost savings would increase impact.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without final commas); standardize punctuation in bullets and section formatting. No obvious misspellings or major typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and anchoring it more directly to public-sector/advocacy digital leadership would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your niche: public-sector, advocacy, and mission-driven digital communications leadership.
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with sharper, outcome-oriented wording.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, CMS modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics that support complex digital operations. Strong track record in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
- “Platform modernization” overlaps with Topline Skills and multiple NACo experience bullets.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize higher-value strategic capabilities over broad or repeated phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic items like “Multi-channel communication” with more specific, senior-level phrasing such as “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Reduce overlap with technical sections by broadening “Web & CMS administration” to “Web platform governance & CMS operations.”
- Combine similar workflow items for clarity: “Editorial workflow design” + “Workflow & systems architecture” → “Editorial operations, workflow design & systems architecture.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS operations • Editorial operations, workflow design & systems architecture • Data analytics, reporting & optimization • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, advocacy messaging, analytics, and multimedia.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills; consider removing if space is tight.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting impact, transformation outcomes, and what is new since returning as a consultant.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal-based campaign delivery, content operations, and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping duties into 3–4 impact bullets; e.g., “Redesigned digital workflows, analytics, and governance to improve cross-channel coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, publishing speed, stakeholder adoption, or reduced support burden.
- Rephrase technical detail to show business value: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval model, structured content requirements, and discovery UX to improve access to policy/member resources.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Campaign/st storytelling experiences within Drupal” overlaps with Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and leave examples to the project section.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement repeat the Director role; emphasize consultant-specific advisory/implementation impact.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize the strongest achievement first: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes sharper where possible: add team size, budget size, reporting cadence, production volume, or efficiency gains from analytics/governance/studio build.
- Condense channel oversight into one line and emphasize transformation: “Expanded analytics across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery; established publishing standards and planning systems to improve reporting and cross-team execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and modernization.
- Video/studio language may overlap with older video-production bullets; stress building organizational capacity, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it sharper by emphasizing what changed under your ownership and adding any concrete audience, cadence, or workflow metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + impact: “Led day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social, and video, scaling NACo’s editorial and advocacy communications operations.”
- Tighten bullets to outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching [X]+ county officials and public-sector stakeholders” and “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace weak phrasing like “helped improve” with ownership verbs: “Built,” “standardized,” “streamlined,” “coordinated,” “institutionalized.”
- Add measurable operational results if available: publishing volume, email growth/open rates, video views, turnaround time, or number of cross-functional teams aligned.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; frame this as scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.
- “Editorial planning/workflows” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; keep this entry focused on execution and operational build-out.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership areas and reduce generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial systems and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content strategy” to sound more senior and aligned with director/consulting work.
- If space allows, make one phrase more distinctive to recent work, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy, governance & modernization.”
- Keep terminology parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also echoes the header and multiple NACo experience bullets; “communications” may fit better than “messaging.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than exhaustive technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is required for target roles.
- Consider replacing “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” with “Multi-platform CMS experience (Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)” to reduce listiness.
- If possible, align with recent impact: prioritize Drupal, CMS modernization, automation, and AI search because those are most supported by 2022–present experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep wording distinct or remove from one section.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery

- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive and leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis**
- Group tools first, then capabilities; remove repeated hyphens and keep parallel phrasing.
- If accurate, strengthen with scope language tied to recent work: **Enterprise analytics infrastructure**, **dashboard development**, or **decision-support reporting**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization**; consider keeping tools there and using this topline item for higher-level capabilities only.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; “SEO, UX and performance analysis” is cleaner and more distinct.

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership and production scope rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task-level skills to higher-value capabilities: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and studio camera operations • In-house studio management”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to align with the Director role and built in-house studio achievement.
- Swap “Hybrid and virtual event production” to “Hybrid event production and livestream operations” for stronger phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If space allows, add scale/context rather than tools: e.g., “Recurring advocacy programming and event broadcasts” instead of generic editing language.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either be tightened or reframed to emphasize depth in the most recent, highest-impact platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize current/recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show level of use: “Drupal (migration, governance, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a notable project; it feels less central than Drupal/SharePoint/Power Pages for this profile.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; “CMS & Web Platforms” may read slightly cleaner than “Web Platforms & CMS.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same core tools.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent NACo roles, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools most tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a tighter, more current list: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Edge/automation: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use versions; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add one specificity cue tied to recent work: “for Drupal-based sites, analytics tagging, and lightweight workflow automation.”
- Order by strongest/recent relevance: JavaScript, API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, then HTML/CSS/jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- If space is tight, keep this section more tool-focused and leave broader capability phrasing to Topline Skills.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since workflow automation is already emphasized elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more clearly grouped by function.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by category to signal systems thinking, e.g.: **Automation & Workflow Systems:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; collaboration platforms: Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Put strongest/relevant tools first: lead with **Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier** because they align with your recent workflow/automation work.
- Consider adding a light qualifier only if true: **“workflow design, task orchestration, and cross-team coordination”** in the heading or nearby skills summary.
- If space is tight, cut lower-value/general tools and keep 5–7 most relevant platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same emphasis without adding specificity.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; they add less differentiation than automation/project-system tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too generic and underplays your recent leadership in email operations. It should signal platform depth and scale without repeating work-experience bullets.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive • Mailchimp”
- If accurate, add scope/context rather than just names: “Enterprise email marketing, member communications, journey automation”
- Consider a stronger label: “Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms” instead of “Email & Engagement Systems”
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, list it first and consider adding proficiency cues, e.g., “Higher Logic Thrive (primary) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding newsletter scale or audience numbers here; that impact is already covered in recent NACo roles.
- Don’t repeat “multi-channel communications” language already emphasized in Core Competencies and Work Experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and anchor it in “firsts,” team-building, and concrete outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand member-facing communications.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervised/mentored a digital media associate” if accurate.
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social performance, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; in this entry, frame it as launching or early producing rather than expanding.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple NACo roles; specify what changed or what channels/processes were newly organized.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the launch and scope, and trim broad support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting program and policy teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer function, e.g., “produced digital and multimedia content to support policy communications and member programs.”
- If possible, add scale or output: number of episodes, audiences served, projects coordinated, or types of stakeholders/program teams supported.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear; one concise sentence or two tight bullets is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; avoid repeating broad multimedia language.
- “Supporting organizational programs and policy work” is generic—use specific program, research, or communications contributions if available.
